models.purpose: Forecast the number of reported results on 1 March 2023 with an interval.
models.summary: ARIMA written as a constant plus an autoregressive sum and a moving-average sum. Order chosen by a stepwise AICc search after one difference, giving (1,1,1). The 90% interval on 1 March 2023 is [10517, 27007] with expected value 16529.

variables.definition: Number of reported results on day t.
One-step prediction of the reported count.

Coefficient on the lagged count.
Coefficient on the lagged residual.
Error term between time t and t-1.
Order of the autoregressive part.
Order of the moving-average part, printed as AM.
Number of differences, fixed at 1.

governing_equations.source_expression: phat_t = p0 + sum gamma_j p_{t-j} + sum theta_j eps_{t-j}
governing_equations.purpose: Prediction equation. The moving-average order is printed as AM.

objectives: Give a 90% interval for the report count on 1 March 2023.
constraints: Only the official contest file is used.
No seasonal term, because the ACF shows none.

details: The series is used from 7 January 2022 to 31 December 2022.

parameter_estimation.method: Stepwise minimization of AICc, a variation of the Hyndman-Khandakar algorithm.

steps: Split the series into training and test sets.
Difference once after the ADF test.
Fit four initial models and search by steps of plus or minus one.
Stop when no lower AICc is found.
Check that the residuals are white noise.
algorithm.convergence_criteria: Repeat until no lower AICc can be found.

assumptions: The statistical laws of the series do not change with time after one difference.
The series is not white noise, since Box-Ljung gives 253.36.

identifiability_feasibility.analysis: Order (1,1,1) minimizes AICc. Residuals pass the Ljung-Box test and a Q-Q plot.

models.computational_cost: One stepwise search over a small set of orders.
strengths: The order is chosen by a stated criterion, not by reading the plots alone.
limitations: The plots are called difficult and subjective, yet three candidate orders are still listed.
missing_details: The software and the exact AICc values are not reported.

models.purpose: Relate word attributes to the share of scores reported in Hard Mode.
models.summary: Five attributes enter a full model. LASSO keeps letter repetitions and frequency. The reduced fit has adjusted R squared printed as Ra2dj 0.782, and both coefficients pass the significance test.

equation_status.reason: Equations (2) to (4) are the regression fits.

objectives: Find which attributes move the Hard Mode share.

details: Each solution word is one observation.

parameter_estimation.method: Ordinary least squares, then LASSO for variable selection.

steps: Compute Pearson correlations.
Fit the five-variable model.
Keep the two variables LASSO selects.
Run the four diagnostic plots and the VIF.
algorithm.convergence_criteria: Adjusted R squared printed as 0.782; VIF below 10.

assumptions: Errors are independent, identical and normal.
No linear relation among the explanatory variables.

identifiability_feasibility.analysis: VIF values 1.166984 and 1.341964, both far below the threshold of 10.

models.computational_cost: One correlation matrix and two linear fits.
strengths: Every regression assumption is checked against a named panel.
limitations: The same symbols X1 and X2 change meaning between equation (2) and equation (3).
missing_details: The LASSO penalty and the significance levels are not printed.

models.purpose: Turn two guessing strategies into distributions of reported results.
models.summary: The tile configuration is reduced to a triple of colour counts, giving 384 states plus a failure state. Two strategies set the opening distribution. Transitions are exponential in the information gain. Reported results are the absorption time.

objectives: Produce a seven-bin distribution under each strategy.
constraints: A player keeps every green tile already earned.

parameter_estimation.method: State information is estimated from the word bank by equation (16), called the Marxian chain.

steps: Reduce the tile set to a colour triple.
Build the reachable states.
Compute the opening distribution for each strategy.
Fill the transition matrix.
Read the absorption time.

assumptions: Players share one word bank and one subjective probability.
The higher the information gain, the lower its probability.

identifiability_feasibility.analysis: The chain is fully specified, but the notation table mis-pairs symbols with descriptions.

models.computational_cost: One pass over about 36,000 words and a 384-state matrix.
strengths: Both strategies are derived from a numbered assumption.
limitations: The reduction throws away which letters were seen, not only how many.
missing_details: The value of C used for the reported distributions is not stated here.

models.family: prototype clustering with a difficulty score
models.purpose: Group solution words by attributes and read the difficulty of each group.
models.summary: A difficulty score weights the seven attempt bins, with seven or more tries counted as 8. K-Prototypes gives three classes. The Kullback-Leibler divergences are 109.59, 271.9 and 864.3, and EERIE is placed in the hard class.

variables.definition: Share of games solved in i tries.
Weighted sum of the seven attempt shares.
Word attributes used for clustering.
Central sample of a cluster.

governing_equations.purpose: Difficulty score. The bin beyond six tries is weighted 8.

objectives: Separate words into difficulty classes using only word attributes.

parameter_estimation.method: Prototypes are recomputed after every assignment.

steps: Pick one prototype per cluster.
Assign each word to the nearest prototype.
Update the prototype.
Repeat until no word changes cluster.
algorithm.convergence_criteria: Stop when no sample changes category.

assumptions: Difficulty depends only on the word itself.
A player who fails does so in about eight guesses, unless the failure is deliberate.

identifiability_feasibility.analysis: Three classes are obtained and EERIE falls in the hard class.

models.computational_cost: One clustering pass over the solution words.
strengths: The classes are described by their centers, not only by a score.
limitations: The number of clusters is not justified against an index.
missing_details: The distance used for mixed attributes is not named.

models.family: strategy mixture with gaussian process regression
models.purpose: Estimate the daily mix of the two strategies and predict it forward.
models.summary: The reported distribution is a mixture of the two strategy distributions. The mix minimizes a cross-entropy, described as similar to maximum likelihood. A Gaussian process predicts the mix on 1 March 2023 as 0.63 with interval [0.59, 0.67].

governing_equations.purpose: Cross-entropy estimate, called similar to maximum likelihood. The printed log has no argument separator.

equation_status.reason: Equations (24) to (29) define the mixture and its estimate.

objectives: Predict the strategy mix and the reported distribution for a future day.
constraints: The two shares sum to one.

details: The mix is estimated day by day from 7 January to 31 December 2022.

parameter_estimation.method: Cross-entropy minimization per day, then Gaussian process regression over the resulting series.

steps: Estimate the daily mix by cross-entropy.
Fit a Gaussian process to the series.
Predict the mix on 1 March 2023.
Combine it with the two strategy distributions.
Repeat at C equal to 1, 2 and 3.

assumptions: The proportion using each strategy is constant within a day.
A Gaussian process prior is appropriate for the mix series.

identifiability_feasibility.analysis: The predicted mix is 0.63. The final distribution is (0.000, 0.148, 11.046, 28.438, 35.456, 21.156, 3.756).

validation_refs: Figure 18: predictions at three values of C.
models.computational_cost: One scalar minimization per day and one Gaussian process fit.
strengths: The mix is estimated from data instead of being fixed.
limitations: Robustness is claimed from one parameter tried at three values.
missing_details: The kernel of the Gaussian process is not stated.

dependency_edges.handoff: The two strategy distributions are the components of the mixture.
The predicted distribution of EERIE is the check for its hard label.
